newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany denies Beirut plastic waste is hazardous.
newsitem.headline: Germany denies Beirut plastic waste is hazardous.

text.p: Environmental watchdog Greenpeace on Wednesday demanded that Germany take back some 680 tonnes of plastic waste which it said were hazardous and had been shipped to Beirut illegally by two German companies.

But German authorities said there was no evidence yet that the consignment contained anything other than its declared contents of waste plastic granulate, which is not hazardous and needs no special permission to be exported.

Greenpeace Lebanon campaigner Fouad Hamdan told a news conference that a Lebanese Environment Ministry report proved that 36 containers seized at Beirut port contained hazardous and unsorted plastic waste that cannot be recycled in Lebanon.

"Greenpeace demands Germany vow to take back the 36 containers. Germany has a moral and legal responsibility to return the mixture of plastic wastes contaminated with labortory chemicals, pesticides and chemical fertilisers," Hamdan added.

Lebanese judicial authorities are investigating the illegal shipment. Environment Minister Pierre Pharaon said on Monday an "international waste mafia" was behind the deal and that Beirut would ask Bonn to take back the containers.

But the environment ministry of Baden-Wuerttemberg state, where the consignment originated, said it had no evidence yet of contamination and was awaiting the result of an examination by a German police officer.

"The investigations by the Duesseldorf state prosecutor will show whether the plastic granulate was contaminated with other materials, and if so, when, where and by whom," the ministry said in a statement.
"So far there is no evidence of any mistake by authorities supervising the legal disposal of waste."

Lebanese prosecutor-general Adnan Addoum, who is heading the investigation, on Tuesday met the German commercial attache in Beirut and said he would get a reply within 48 hours from the Germans on whether they would take back the waste.
Hamdan said the 36 containers were shipped to Beirut by German firms International Trade and Finance in Saulheim and RC Reifenrecycling in Hagen.

"Two main reasons qualify this operation to be illegal traffic under the Basel Convention. First, the operation took place without the consent of the Lebanese authorities. Second, the hazardous waste does not conform with the material declared officially in the bill of lading," Hamdan added.
The shipment was declared as plastic raw material for industrial production but the Lebanese company that was to buy it rejected the material when it realised that it was useless waste, he added.
